messages:
devon: FYI running a stress run on the dedicated pool (32xA100-ish) and hit repeating p99 spikes when concurrency > 480. p50 stable ~75ms but p99 jumps to ~880ms. looks correlated with KV cache evictions and a kernel fallback path.
marta: can you paste the profiler output? is it KV eviction causing waits or kernel kernel-selection stalls?
devon: attaching salient bits below. noticed: bursts of eviction followed by a chain of microbatch size reductions and then we hit a slow kernel path. logs:
```
[12:07:31] evict: model=redwood/opt-3b hotset=0.62 reason=kv_pressure free=14% slot=45
[12:07:31] mb_adjust: incoming_q=512 -> microbatch=1 (hysteresis_trigger)
[12:07:31] kernel_switch: chosen=fast_attention_v2 fallback=matmul_impl delay_ms=23
[12:07:32] response_latency p99=880ms p50=72ms
```
priya: hmm microbatch dropping to 1 on that workload is bad — it kills batching efficiency; why is hysteresis firing so aggressively?
devon: current heuristic: if free_kv_slots < 20% OR evictions/sec > 5 then set microbatch_min=1. clearly too brittle under bursty qps. bench-bot run metadata: 500 qps sustained for 6m with 2s tail-k queries.
bench-bot: synthetic-run: id=run-2026-03-12-17 qps=500 duration=360s evictions_total=4.1k avg_mb=2.1 p99=880ms link=https://bench.internal/203345/run-2026-03-12
tom: two angles: 1) make eviction threshold adaptive with short-term smoothing (ewma) so single spikes don't drop mb to 1; 2) decouple kernel selection decision from instantaneous kv pressure so we don't pick the slow fallback during transient stress.
marta: +1. also we should consider pinning a small hotset for top-x requests per model for a short TTL to prevent churn.
priya: proposed config patch (quick sketch):
```
kv:
  eviction:
    window_secs: 10
    ewma_alpha: 0.2
    pressure_high: 0.65
    pressure_low: 0.45
microbatch:
  min: 2
  max: 32
  reduce_step: 1
  hysteresis_cooldown_ms: 500
kernel:
  prefer_fast_for_mb_ge: 4
  fallback_delay_ms: 50
```
devon: implemented a local variant of that and re-ran -> p99 dropped to 210ms under same synthetic load, evictions still happened but no microbatch collapse. flamegraph: https://perf.internal/fg/203345 (captures kernel stalls + syscalls)
marta: nice. can you open a short PR with the config default changes and a comment in the kernel selector? also we need an experiment to sweep prefer_fast_for_mb_ge between 2..8.
devon: will do. also noticed one more thing: in the flamegraph there's a 18ms tail in cuda memcpy that lines up with eviction notification processing. we might batch eviction updates on the control plane thread.
priya: batching eviction notifications and applying them every 10-20ms could smooth control churn. but need to measure memory pressure semantics.
tom: action items: (1) devon PR with config + notes (2) marta to run sweep for prefer_fast_for_mb_ge (3) priya prototype eviction-notify batching (4) bench-bot run the 1h stress with new defaults and post results. I'll create tasks.
bench-bot: scheduled job: stress-203345-adaptive-config queued; ETA ~45m.
sre-bot: deploy-check: config change touches runtime defaults; ensure canary on 1 shard with traffic mirroring before wide rollout.
devon: noted. I'll push PR and add canary annotation. thanks all :thumbsup:
